wording: Do you consider yourself a supporter to any particular political party? If so, do you feel yourself to be very involved in this party, fairly involved or merely a sympathizer?
categories: 1 very involved; 2 fairly involved; 3 merely a sympathizer; 4 no affinities with any party; 8 DK/NA; 9 inap
note: Supporter/involvement wording. Not the same stimulus as the closeness wording that replaces it.

wording: Do you consider yourself to be close to any particular party? <IF YES> Do you feel yourself to be very close to this party, fairly close or merely a sympathizer?
categories: 1 very close; 2 fairly close; 3 merely a sympathizer; 4 close to no particular party; 8 DK/NA; 9 inap
note: English versions ask an ABSOLUTE question, French-derived versions a RELATIVE one ('closer to one party than to the others'). Codebook fn. 119.

wording: <Follow-up question after the respondents have been asked to choose a party to which they feel close to> Do you consider yourself to be very close to this party, fairly close or merely a sympathizer?
note: Question ORDER break, not a wording break: attachment is asked after the party has already been named.
EB39, EB40, EB41 not asked in Finland; EB42 not asked in Finland, Sweden and Austria (codebook fn. 120).

wording: Generally speaking, do you feel closer to one of the <national> political parties than the others? If yes, which one?
note: Note this is the RELATIVE form, in English. In ECS73 it was used in place of vote intention.

wording: Generally speaking, which political party do you feel closer to?
note: EB29 asked in Ireland and Northern Ireland only.

wording: <To those who say code 1 (very close), 2 (fairly close) or 3 (merely a sympathiser) in CLOSEPTY> To which party do you feel close?
note: Filtered on closepty, so it identifies the party of attached respondents only.

wording: If there were a 'general election' tomorrow (say if contact is under 18 years: and you had a vote), which party would you support?
categories: country-specific party codes; 990 other; 995 blank/spoilt; 996 would not vote; 997 refused; 998 DK; 999 inap
note: EB41 onward say 'vote for' rather than 'support'. Many country-specific code collapses -- see codebook fn. 125.

wording: <If DK or NA in VOTEINT> Which party would you be inclined to vote for?
note: A follow-up on the VOTE item, not on attachment. Asked only in GB/IRL/NIRL for several waves.

wording: Which party did you vote for at the last general election in (year of last general election)?
note: Earlier waves are country-restricted: EB18-27 Belgium only, EB24-29 Spain and Portugal only.

wording: Are you yourself or is someone in your household a member of a political party?
note: Only the respondent-is-member category is in the trend file. Substantive answers 1988-1991 only.

wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale?
note: Not a partisanship item; carried for context.

wording: Do you consider yourself to be close to any particular party? If so, do you feel yourself to be very close to this party, fairly close, or merely a sympathizer?
categories: 1 very involved; 2 fairly involved; 3 merely sympathizer; 4 no affinities with any party
note: The xlsx gives the CLOSENESS wording but the delivered value labels are the INVOLVEMENT ones, i.e. the EB4-EB9 family. Treat the 2009 point as not strictly comparable to 1978-1994.

wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale?
note: Not a partisanship item; carried for context.

wording: Supposing a (national/general election) were being held tomorrow, can you tell me on a scale of 1 to 10 how likely it is that you would vote in that election?
note: Turnout propensity, not party choice.
No partisanship item. attach_cntry / attach_eur are attachment to COUNTRY and to EUROPE, not to a party. Redundant with the harmonised file.
NO closeness, affinity or attachment item exists anywhere in the CEEB trend file. The construct was never fielded in Central and Eastern Europe under this instrument.

wording: <Ask only those of voting age> Do you have the right to vote in (our country) at General Elections?
categories: 1 have right; 2 do not have right; 8 DK; 9 NA
note: Filter for the vote-intention items.

wording: If there was a 'General Election' today (say if contact under voting age or not allowed to vote 'and you had a vote'), would you go and vote in the next 'General Election'?
categories: 1 yes I would vote; 2 no I would not vote; 8 DK; 9 no answer
note: Substantive answers in 1991-1993 only, and not for every country.

wording: <Ask only those who have right to vote> If there were a general election tomorrow, which party or block would you vote for, or might you be inclined to vote for?
note: One column PER COUNTRY (V79-V100 intention, V101-V117 inclination); they must be coalesced before use.

wording: And which party did you vote for on <date of last election>?
note: GDR 1990 (Volkskammerwahl) in the documented wave.
